Chaldea
kal-DEE-uh
proper noun / place
From Hebrew Kasdīm (Chaldeans/Chaldea); the land and people of southern Mesopotamia, associated with Babylon, Ur, and the instrument of Judah’s exile.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Chaldea is the land of the Chaldeans, the Mesopotamian power-sphere tied to Ur of the Chaldees, to Babylon’s rise, and to the rod of the LORD’s anger against Judah. Abram was called out of Ur of the Chaldees; centuries later the Chaldeans come up against Jerusalem as the appointed instrument of judgment. Chaldea is therefore both origin and scourge in redemptive history: the old country left by faith, and the empire that empties Zion under wrath. The prophets do not flatter Chaldea. They name her pride, her idols, and her appointed hour, and they also promise her fall when the cup is finished. Modern discourse often reduces Chaldea to museum archaeology or astrology branding. Scripture presents a moral empire under God. Hold Chaldea, and hold the double lesson of election and judgment: God calls a man out of the Chaldees, and God later raises the Chaldeans to chasten His people, then breaks the rod. Geography is theology when the LORD writes both call and captivity across the same name. The name stands in Scripture so that the church will not invent a thinner story than the one God wrote in places and persons under providence.

Webster 1828 Definition

Land of the Chaldeans; Mesopotamian sphere of Ur, Babylon, and Judah’s exile under God.

expand to see more

CHALDEA, the land of the Chaldeans in southern Mesopotamia.

Ur of the Chaldees is Abram’s old country.

The Chaldeans become Babylon’s rod against Judah.

Prophets announce both their rise as judgment and their fall.

The name binds call, captivity, and divine sovereignty.

Key Scripture

Gen 11:28 — "And Haran died before his father Terah in the land of his nativity, in Ur of the Chaldees."

Gen 15:7 — "And he said unto him, I am the LORD that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it."

Hab 1:6 — "For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs."

Isa 13:19 — "And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah."

Modern Corruption

Chaldea is museumized or astrologized; Scripture makes it origin of call and rod of judgment under God.

expand to see more

The corruption is to treat Chaldea as neutral ancient culture. Scripture pairs Ur with call and Chaldeans with wrath. Recover moral geography under the LORD.

A second misuse is fatalism: empires just happen. Habakkuk hears God raise the Chaldeans. Recover sovereignty without excusing their evil.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Chaldea is the Chaldean land: Abram’s Ur behind him and Babylon’s rod before Judah.

expand to see more

Hebrew — Kasdim / Chaldeans.

Origin — Ur of the Chaldees.

Empire — Babylon’s Chaldean power.

Function — rod of judgment; then judged.

Doctrine — call and captivity under one Lord.

Usage

"The LORD brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees."

"God raised up the Chaldeans as a bitter and hasty nation."

"Babylon is the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency under doom."
